2607.09400.title: On-Device Adaptive Battery Power Prediction for Electric Vehicles
2607.09400.paper_summary: Adaptive power management in Electric Vehicles (EVs) requires accurate power prediction. Although deep learning models have emerged as highly effective for time-series forecasting in this domain, their performance is prone to degradation when exposed to data with distributions different from the training data. We introduce a novel approach that enables on-device learning in resource-constrained EV systems to continuously adapt pretrained battery prediction models to new, unseen data. We leverage existing pretrained models by transforming them into adaptable versions that retain critical hyperparameter knowledge from their initial training. We comprehensively investigate both online and offline model adaptation strategies. Our results demonstrate significant improvements in forecasting performance across various models and time horizons, achieving mean absolute error reductions of up to 7.49\% and 14.88\% with online and offline adaptation techniques, respectively. This study highlights the substantial benefit of on-device adaptation, resulting in enhanced battery power predictions than unadapted model deployments in real-world EV scenarios.
2607.09400.paper_summary_zh: 適應性電力管理在電動車（EV）中需要準確的電力預測。儘管深度學習模型已被證明在此領域的時間序列預測中非常有效，但當面對與訓練數據分佈不同的數據時，它們的性能容易下降。我們提出了一種新穎的方法，使資源受限的電動車系統能夠在設備上進行學習，持續地將預訓練的電池預測模型適應於新的、未見過的數據。我們通過將現有的預訓練模型轉換為可適應的版本來利用它們，這些版本保留了其初始訓練中的關鍵超參數知識。我們全面研究了在線和離線模型適應策略。我們的結果顯示，在各種模型和時間範圍內，預測性能顯著改善，通過在線和離線適應技術，平均絕對誤差分別降低了高達7.49\%和14.88\%。這項研究突顯了設備上適應的重大好處，使得電池電力預測比在現實世界電動車場景中未適應的模型部署更為精確。
